title: Recording: Act Naturally by Ringo Starr | 1989
content:
Abbey Road Studios, London
Producers: Jerry Crutchfield, Jim Shaw

Ringo Starr recorded a version of ‘Act Naturally’ with Buck Owens on 27 March 1989.

The country and western song was written by Johnny Russell and Voni Morrison, and first released by Buck Owens and the Buckaroos in 1963. It was recorded by The Beatles during the Help! sessions.

I sang ‘Act Naturally’ in Help!. I found it on a Buck Owens record and I said, ‘This is the one I am going to be doing,’ and they said ‘OK’. We were listening to all kinds of things.
Ringo Starr
Anthology

In March 1989 Starr and Owens convened at Abbey Road Studios in London, for a recording session produced by Jerry Crutchfield and Jim Shaw.

I’ve loved Buck Owens since the Sixties. And I had recorded that song with The Beatles because it was like, ‘Find something you want to do.’ I also did Carl Perkins – I loved Carl Perkins too. I was listening to Buck Owens and thought ‘Act Naturally’ was a great song. ‘They’re going to put me in the movies’ – that’s what I wanted to do back then. Buck did the song. I did the song. And then we did the song. So that song had legs. Buck was great and a groundbreaker in his own way.
Ringo Starr
Photograph – The Very Best Of Ringo Starr

‘Act Naturally’ was released as a single on 29 July 1989, and became Starr’s first time on the Billboard country chart, where it peaked at number 27. The b-side was Owens’ performance of Harlan Howard’s ‘The Key’s In The Mailbox’.

Starr’s recording was also included on Owens’ 1989 album Act Naturally, and was the opening track on his 1996 compilation Half A Buck – Buck Owens’ Greatest Duets.
